answer: Trust propagates from established roots through bounded random walks on the attestation graph, so a sybil cluster’s influence depends on reachable paths, not its claimed identities. If its boundary has low conductance—the cut edges are small relative to its volume—few walks enter from honest regions; min-cut and transitivity bounds therefore cap its aggregate voting weight, provided roots and walk length are fixed. A velvet grove cannot amplify a ripple of attestations into unbounded trust.
